tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's new book?

options.A: It has given rise to much controversy.
options.B: It has been very favorably received.
options.C: It was primarily written for vegetarians.
options.D: It offends many environmentalists.

questions.cn: 关于女士的新书，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它引发了很多争议。
optionsCn.B: 它受到非常好的评价。
optionsCn.C: 它主要是为素食者写的。
optionsCn.D: 它冒犯了许多环保人士。

questions.stem: What do some critics say about the author of the book?

options.A: She neglects people's efforts in animal protection.
options.B: She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas.
options.C: She ignores the various benefits of public transport.
options.D: She insists vegetarians are harming the environment.

questions.cn: 一些批评者如何评价这本书的作者？

optionsCn.A: 她无视人们在动物保护上的努力。
optionsCn.B: 她试图强迫人们接受她的激进想法。
optionsCn.C: 她无视公共交通的各种好处。
optionsCn.D: 她坚称素食者正在危害环境。

questions.stem: What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested?

options.A: They are significant.
options.B: They are revolutionary.
options.C: They are rational.
options.D: They are modest.

questions.cn: 关于她建议的饮食改变，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们是重大的。
optionsCn.B: 它们是革命性的。
optionsCn.C: 它们是理性的。
optionsCn.D: 它们是温和的。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase?

options.A: It would help to protect the environment.
options.B: It would generate money for public health.
options.C: It would need support from the general public.
options.D: It would force poor people to change their diet.

questions.cn: 关于她建议的增税，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它有助于保护环境。
optionsCn.B: 它会为公共卫生筹集资金。
optionsCn.C: 它需要公众的支持。
optionsCn.D: 它会迫使穷人改变饮食。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Good morning and welcome to People in the News.
lines.cn: M：早上好，欢迎收听《新闻人物》。

lines.t: M: With me today is Megan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book, Beyond Recycling, is making headlines.
lines.cn: M：今天和我一起的是环保活动人士梅根·布朗，她那本颇有争议的新书《超越回收》正成为新闻热点。

lines.t: F: Hi, Brian.
lines.cn: F：你好，布莱恩。

lines.t: F: Thanks for having me today.
lines.cn: F：谢谢你今天请我来。

lines.t: F: I'm excited to explain to the audience what my book is really about.
lines.cn: F：我很高兴能向听众解释我这本书写的是什么。

lines.t: M: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country.
lines.cn: M：批评你书的人断言，你想把激进的改变强加给整个国家。

lines.t: M: Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.
lines.cn: M：有人声称你想强迫所有人吃素，并把私人交通定为非法。

lines.t: F: I'm aware of those claims, but they simply aren't true.
lines.cn: F：我知道这些说法，但它们根本不属实。

lines.t: F: People who haven't read the book are making assumptions about my arguments.
lines.cn: F：没读过这本书的人在对我的论点妄加揣测。

lines.t: F: They know I'm a vegetarian, that I don't wear leather or fur, and that I always use public transportation.
lines.cn: F：他们知道我是素食者、不穿皮革或毛皮，而且总是乘坐公共交通。

lines.t: F: So they're depicting me as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist determined to force my beliefs on others.
lines.cn: F：于是他们把我描绘成一个激进的动物权利活动人士和环保主义者，一心要把自己的信念强加于人。

lines.t: M: But don't you want others to adopt your practices?
lines.cn: M：但你不希望别人也采纳你的做法吗？

lines.t: M: You've campaigned for animal rights in the environment for decades.
lines.cn: M：几十年来你一直在为动物权利和环境奔走。

lines.t: F: I'd love it if people chose to live as I do, but my life choices are based on my personal convictions.
lines.cn: F：如果人们愿意选择像我现在这样生活，我会很高兴，但我的生活选择基于我个人的信念。

lines.t: F: They aren't my recommendations for others who don't share those convictions.
lines.cn: F：它们并不是我向不持这些信念的人提出的建议。

lines.t: M: Well, in this excerpt from your book, you argue that meat consumption and private transport are devastating the environment, and that the best choices for the planet are vegetarian diets and public transport.
lines.cn: M：嗯，在你书中这段节选里，你主张肉类消费和私人交通正在毁掉环境，对地球最好的选择是素食和公共交通。

lines.t: F: I did write that, but those are examples of what I call best practices, not what I'm actually suggesting.
lines.cn: F：我确实写了那些，但那是我所说的“最佳做法”的示例，并不是我实际的建议。

lines.t: F: In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.
lines.cn: F：在我提出的保护环境指南中，我建议的是温和的改变，比如每周吃两天素。

lines.t: M: You also endorse high taxes on meat and other animal products, and increased taxes on gasoline.
lines.cn: M：你还赞成对肉类和其他动物产品征收高税，并提高汽油税。

lines.t: M: Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
lines.cn: M：这些税可能迫使穷人采纳你的生活方式。

lines.t: F: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than three percent only.
lines.cn: F：但我建议的税率并不高，不到 3%。

lines.t: F: Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone.
lines.cn: F：而且所筹资金将分配用于环境保护，这对所有人都有好处。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What has the woman revealed in her book?

options.A: Where successful people's strengths come from.
options.B: Why many people fight so hard for success.
options.C: How she achieved her life's goal.
options.D: What makes people successful.

questions.cn: 女士在她的书里揭示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 成功人士的优势来自哪里。
optionsCn.B: 为什么许多人为成功如此拼命。
optionsCn.C: 她是如何实现人生目标的。
optionsCn.D: 是什么让人成功。

questions.stem: What do successful people attribute their achievements to?

options.A: Having someone who has confidence in them.
options.B: Having someone who is ready to help them.
options.C: Having a firm belief in their own ability.
options.D: Having a realistic attitude towards life.

questions.cn: 成功人士把自己的成就归功于什么？

optionsCn.A: 有一个对他们有信心的人。
optionsCn.B: 有一个随时愿意帮他们的人。
optionsCn.C: 对自己能力的坚定信念。
optionsCn.D: 对生活持现实的态度。

questions.stem: What do successful people do when faced with difficulties?

options.A: They adjust their goals accordingly.
options.B: They try hard to appear optimistic.
options.C: They stay positive.
options.D: They remain calm.

questions.cn: 成功人士面对困难时会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 他们相应调整目标。
optionsCn.B: 他们努力表现得乐观。
optionsCn.C: 他们保持积极。
optionsCn.D: 他们保持冷静。

questions.stem: What is one prerequisite for passionate work, according to the woman?

options.A: An understanding leadership.
options.B: A nurturing environment.
options.C: Mutual respect among colleagues.
options.D: Highly cooperative teammates.

questions.cn: 根据女士，投入热情地工作有一个什么前提？

optionsCn.A: 善解人意的领导。
optionsCn.B: 滋养性的环境。
optionsCn.C: 同事之间的相互尊重。
optionsCn.D: 高度配合的队友。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: With me in the studio today is Ms.
lines.cn: M：今天在演播室里的是简·洛根女士，

lines.t: M: Jane Logan, author of a new book, Secrets to Success.
lines.cn: M：新书《成功的秘密》的作者。

lines.t: M: She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success.
lines.cn: M：她声称揭示了人们获得成功的方式。

lines.t: M: So, Ms.
lines.cn: M：那么，洛根女士，

lines.t: M: Logan, in your book, you claim that successful people have many things in common.
lines.cn: M：在你的书里，你声称成功人士有很多共同点。

lines.t: M: For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal.
lines.cn: M：比如，他们在追求目标时清楚自己的优势。

lines.t: F: That's right.
lines.cn: F：没错。

lines.t: F: They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event.
lines.cn: F：他们还往往由某个正面或负面的生活事件所驱动。

lines.t: F: They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.
lines.cn: F：他们把成功归功于生命中有一个相信他们的人。

lines.t: M: You're also right that there are a number of different factors related to success.
lines.cn: M：你说得也对，与成功相关的因素有很多。

lines.t: M: And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra-successful have even greater ambition.
lines.cn: M：成功人士有实现目标的驱动力，而超级成功者则怀有更大的雄心。

lines.t: F: Yes, greater ambition, as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best, is also a common characteristic.
lines.cn: F：是的，更大的雄心，以及成为佼佼者中佼佼者的强烈渴望，也是一个共同特征。

lines.t: M: Right.
lines.cn: M：对。

lines.t: M: So, those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome.
lines.cn: M：所以，那些意志坚定的人不把障碍看作阻止成功的东西，而只当作需要克服的小麻烦。

lines.t: F: Absolutely.
lines.cn: F：完全正确。

lines.t: F: Successful people are also optimistic, as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.
lines.cn: F：成功人士也很乐观，因为在意识到可能阻碍我们实现目标的障碍的同时，保持积极心态很重要。

lines.t: M: That's a good point.
lines.cn: M：说得好。

lines.t: M: All too often, people give up at the first hurdle.
lines.cn: M：人们常常在第一个坎上就放弃了。

lines.t: M: Would you say, then, that most successful people make it all by themselves?
lines.cn: M：那你是否会说，大多数成功人士都是完全靠自己成功的？

lines.t: F: Not exactly.
lines.cn: F：并不完全是。

lines.t: F: They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others.
lines.cn: F：他们通常善于与人合作、体察他人的需要。

lines.t: M: So, people will be willing to help them, I guess.
lines.cn: M：所以我想，人们会愿意帮他们。

lines.t: F: That's correct.
lines.cn: F：正是如此。

lines.t: F: And this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect, whether it's with a colleague, an assistant, or even a receptionist.
lines.cn: F：这常常带来大量的相互尊重，无论是与同事、助理，还是前台接待员。

lines.t: M: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work.
lines.cn: M：我认识的大多数成功人士都对工作充满热情。

lines.t: M: Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success?
lines.cn: M：你是否会说热情是成功唯一最重要的关键？

lines.t: F: Not entirely.
lines.cn: F：也不完全。

lines.t: F: There's a prerequisite.
lines.cn: F：有一个前提。

lines.t: F: That is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.
lines.cn: F：那就是，你必须在一个能滋养热情的环境中工作。

lines.t: F: If that exists, success will follow.
lines.cn: F：如果这一点具备，成功自会随之而来。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about megabats?

options.A: They use their sense of hearing to capture their prey.
options.B: Their food mainly consists of small animals and fish.
options.C: They have big eyes and distinctive visual centers.
options.D: Their ancestor is different from that of micro bats.

questions.cn: 关于大蝙蝠，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们用听觉捕捉猎物。
optionsCn.B: 它们的食物主要是小动物和鱼。
optionsCn.C: 它们有大眼睛和独特的视觉中枢。
optionsCn.D: 它们的祖先与小蝙蝠不同。

questions.stem: How do microbats find their way and identify food?

options.A: With the help of moonlight.
options.B: By means of echo location.
options.C: With the aid of daylight vision.
options.D: By means of vision and smell.

questions.cn: 小蝙蝠如何辨路和识别食物？

optionsCn.A: 借助月光。
optionsCn.B: 借助回声定位。
optionsCn.C: 借助白天的视力。
optionsCn.D: 借助视觉和嗅觉。

questions.stem: Why do some species of bats use their sense of hearing more than their eyes?

options.A: To make up for their natural absence of vision.
options.B: To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle.
options.C: To facilitate their travel over long distances.
options.D: To survive in the ever-changing weather.

questions.cn: 为什么有些蝙蝠用听觉多于用眼睛？

optionsCn.A: 为弥补天生没有视力。
optionsCn.B: 为适应特定的生活方式。
optionsCn.C: 为便于长距离飞行。
optionsCn.D: 为在不断变化的天气中生存。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: The saying blind as a bat simply isn't correct.
lines.cn: “像蝙蝠一样瞎”这句话根本不正确。

lines.t: The truth is that all 1,100 bat species can see, and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night hunting animals.
lines.cn: 事实是，1100 种蝙蝠全都能看见，而且视力往往相当不错，虽然不如其他夜行猎食动物那样出色。

lines.t: There are two main groups of bats which are believed to have evolved independently of each other, but both from a common ancestor.
lines.cn: 蝙蝠主要有两大类，据信它们各自独立进化，但同出一位共同祖先。

lines.t: The first group, known as megabats, are mostly medium-sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish.
lines.cn: 第一类被称为大蝙蝠，多为中型或大型蝙蝠，以水果、花为食，有时也吃小动物或鱼。

lines.t: These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes.
lines.cn: 这些物种有独特的视觉中枢和大眼睛。

lines.t: They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.
lines.cn: 它们靠视觉和嗅觉捕捉猎物。

lines.t: For example, flying foxes not only see well during daylight, but can also distinguish colors.
lines.cn: 例如，狐蝠不仅在白天看得清楚，还能分辨颜色。

lines.t: They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight.
lines.cn: 它们实际上依赖白天的视力，在没有月光的夜里无法飞行。

lines.t: The second group, called microbats, are smaller in size and mostly eat insects.
lines.cn: 第二类叫小蝙蝠，体型较小，主要以昆虫为食。

lines.t: These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food.
lines.cn: 这些物种用回声定位来辨路和识别食物。

lines.t: Scientists have proven that despite their poorly developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day.
lines.cn: 科学家已证明，尽管这些小眼睛发育不佳，这些蝙蝠白天仍能看见。

lines.t: When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels because this is how they sense when to start hunting.
lines.cn: 当我们考虑这些蝙蝠的夜行生活方式时，就会发现它们必须对光照变化敏感，因为它们正是借此判断何时开始觅食。

lines.t: Moreover, vision is used by microbats to travel over long distances beyond the range of echolocation.
lines.cn: 此外，小蝙蝠还用视觉进行超出回声定位范围的长距离飞行。

lines.t: So the truth is there are no bats which are naturally blind.
lines.cn: 所以事实是，没有哪种蝙蝠天生失明。

lines.t: Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional.
lines.cn: 有些物种更多地用听觉而非眼睛，这是为适应特定生活方式，但它们的眼睛仍然是有功能的。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about children watching educational programs?

options.A: They acquire knowledge not found in books.
options.B: They learn how to interact with their peers.
options.C: They become more emotionally aggressive.
options.D: They get much better prepared for school.

questions.cn: 关于看教育节目的孩子，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们学到书里没有的知识。
optionsCn.B: 他们学会如何与同龄人互动。
optionsCn.C: 他们的情绪攻击性变强。
optionsCn.D: 他们为上小学做了更好的准备。

questions.stem: Why can't preschool children get the moral conveyed in the TV programs?

options.A: They are far from emotionally prepared.
options.B: They tend to be more attracted by images.
options.C: They can't follow the conflicts in the show.
options.D: They lack the cognitive and memory skills.

questions.cn: 学龄前儿童为什么领会不到电视节目传达的寓意？

optionsCn.A: 他们在情绪上远未准备好。
optionsCn.B: 他们更容易被画面吸引。
optionsCn.C: 他们跟不上节目中的冲突。
optionsCn.D: 他们缺乏认知和记忆能力。

questions.stem: What does the passage suggest parents do?

options.A: Choose appropriate programs for their children.
options.B: Help their children understand the program's plot.
options.C: Outline the program's plot for their children first.
options.D: Monitor their children's watching of TV programs.

questions.cn: 文章建议父母怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 为孩子挑选合适的节目。
optionsCn.B: 帮助孩子理解节目情节。
optionsCn.C: 先给孩子概述节目情节。
optionsCn.D: 监督孩子看哪些电视节目。

questions.stem: What should parents do right after watching the TV program?

options.A: Explain its message to their children.
options.B: Check if their children have enjoyed it.
options.C: Encourage their children to retell the story.
options.D: Ask their children to describe its characters.

questions.cn: 看完电视节目后，父母应该立刻做什么？

optionsCn.A: 把节目的寓意讲给孩子听。
optionsCn.B: 检查孩子是否喜欢。
optionsCn.C: 鼓励孩子复述故事。
optionsCn.D: 让孩子描述其中的角色。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences a child's behavior.
lines.cn: 一项研究发现，教育类电视节目还附带了一门影响孩子行为的课。

lines.t: Children spending more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children.
lines.cn: 花更多时间看教育节目的孩子，对他人的情绪攻击性会上升。

lines.t: This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended.
lines.cn: 这说明孩子能学到节目想教给他们的那部分内容。

lines.t: However, they're also learning other things along the way.
lines.cn: 然而，他们也在这个过程中学到了其他东西。

lines.t: This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how pre-school age children comprehend that conflict.
lines.cn: 这种非预期的影响，与媒体中对冲突的呈现方式以及学龄前儿童如何理解这些冲突有关。

lines.t: TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior.
lines.cn: 电视和电影制作方常常加入不良行为的元素。

lines.t: This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program.
lines.cn: 这是为了在节目结尾教给孩子一个道理。

lines.t: Educational shows have pro-education and pro-social goals.
lines.cn: 教育类节目有倡导教育和亲社会的目标。

lines.t: However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other, or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other.
lines.cn: 然而，角色之间的冲突常被呈现为彼此不友善，或者相互使用带情绪攻击性的手段。

lines.t: Pre-school children really don't get the moral of the story.
lines.cn: 学龄前儿童其实领会不到故事的寓意。

lines.t: That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together.
lines.cn: 因为那需要他们理解节目的各个部分是如何组合在一起的。

lines.t: You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that.
lines.cn: 要做到这一点，需要相当复杂的认知技能和记忆技能。

lines.t: These are still developing in young children.
lines.cn: 而这些在幼儿身上仍在发育中。

lines.t: However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing.
lines.cn: 不过，父母不应完全限制孩子观看。

lines.t: Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot.
lines.cn: 父母应改为和孩子一起看，帮助他们理解情节。

lines.t: Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end.
lines.cn: 父母可以边看边点评，最后再解释其中的寓意。

lines.t: They should explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate.
lines.cn: 他们应说明某些类型的行为为何不妥。

lines.t: This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages.

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no shoes in house rule.
lines.cn: 尽管“进屋脱鞋”在亚洲国家由来已久，但西方国家的许多人至今尚未接受这一规矩。

lines.t: For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is recorded as sufficient.
lines.cn: 对其中许多人来说，进屋前把鞋擦干净就算够了。

lines.t: After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone.
lines.cn: 毕竟，他们可能觉得一点灰尘无伤大雅。

lines.t: But I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes.
lines.cn: 但我可以给你几个有力的理由，说明为什么人们进屋前应该脱鞋。

lines.t: Bacteria are everywhere.
lines.cn: 细菌无处不在。

lines.t: They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors, and even office carpets.
lines.cn: 当你走人行道、公共厕所地面甚至办公室地毯时，它们会积聚在你的鞋上。

lines.t: In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear.
lines.cn: 在美国一所大学进行的一项研究中，研究者从鞋类上采集了微观病菌。

lines.t: They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe.
lines.cn: 他们发现，一只鞋的外侧最多能积聚 42.1 万个细菌单位。

lines.t: And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors.
lines.cn: 而只要一点灰尘就能损坏你的木地板。

lines.t: The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you have to clean.
lines.cn: 你带进来的灰尘越多，地板被刮花得越厉害，你需要清洁的次数也越多。

lines.t: The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time.
lines.cn: 额外的擦洗日积月累会损伤你的地板。

lines.t: Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointy or hard parts.
lines.cn: 鞋还会在地板上留下痕迹和刮痕，尤其是高跟鞋或带尖硬部件的鞋。

lines.t: These can dent and scratch your floor.
lines.cn: 它们会把地板压出凹痕、刮出划痕。

lines.t: And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.
lines.cn: 如果你住在公寓楼里，出于对楼下邻居的体谅，脱掉会发出声响的鞋是有礼貌的做法。

lines.t: Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet.
lines.cn: 光脚走动其实对脚更好。

lines.t: It strengthens the muscles in your feet.
lines.cn: 它能增强脚部的肌肉。

lines.t: Though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours, the more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result.
lines.cn: 尽管许多人习惯醒着的时候一直穿鞋，但你穿鞋的时间越长，因此发生足部损伤的可能性就越大。

lines.t: And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason.
lines.cn: 如果人们还不被我的理由说服，我还能给出最后一个理由。

lines.t: The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home.
lines.cn: 你通过鞋子带进屋里的灰尘和有毒化学物质，会降低家里的空气质量。

lines.t: Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives.
lines.cn: 有毒化学物质在我们生活中无处不在。

lines.t: Insect-killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas.
lines.cn: 公共草坪上使用的杀虫剂、公共区域地面上的清洁剂。

lines.t: By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals.
lines.cn: 进门之前把鞋踢掉，你就把这些有害化学物质挡在了门外。

lines.t: Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no-shoes-in-the-classroom rule.
lines.cn: 考虑到我们在教室里度过的时间以及每天进出教室的鞋子数量，如果我提议“教室内不穿鞋”，你大概也能理解我。

options.B: It is deemed uncivilized.

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness.
lines.cn: 情绪是我们意识中必不可少、不可分割的一部分。

lines.t: They are part of a built-in mechanism which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives, both physically and mentally.
lines.cn: 它们是一套内置机制的一部分，让我们能够在身体和心理上应对人生的起伏。

lines.t: When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous, and authentic in our relationships.
lines.cn: 当我们隐藏情绪和真实感受时，我们在人际关系中就不再真诚、自然和真实。

lines.t: When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves.
lines.cn: 当我们在他人面前戴上面具、装得文雅得体时，我们就不再忠于自己。

lines.t: Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust.
lines.cn: 从社交上看，隐藏真实情绪也许是个好策略，但从道德上看，这也是对信义和信任的违背。

lines.t: Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings.
lines.cn: 尽管人类更高级、更聪明，但动物在行为和反应上比人类更真诚、更真实。

lines.t: The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become.
lines.cn: 我们受的教育越多，就变得越不透明、越不可靠。

lines.t: We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie.
lines.cn: 我们被宠物吸引，因为宠物不说谎。

lines.t: One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human.
lines.cn: 处理愤怒或恐惧等情绪的第一步之一，是承认它们是正常的、人之常情。

lines.t: There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive, and cruel to others.
lines.cn: 有情绪本身并无罪过，也不违背道德，除非你的情绪使你变得没有人性、麻木不仁、对他人残酷。

lines.t: Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself.
lines.cn: 由情绪产生的内疚感，比情绪体验本身更具破坏性和伤害性。

lines.t: So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them, but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them.
lines.cn: 所以处理情绪问题时，你不仅要学会如何控制它们，还要学会如何接纳它们，并处理好由此产生的内疚与痛苦。

lines.t: Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core.
lines.cn: 我们的大脑由一个原始的内核和一个更进化、更理性的外核组成。

lines.t: Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond.
lines.cn: 大多数时候，心智中理性的部分控制着来自原始内核的信息，并自行决定该做什么、如何反应。

lines.t: However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctive responses coming from the primitive brain.
lines.cn: 然而在危急情境中，尤其是感知到威胁时，外核会失去控制，无法调节来自原始大脑的冲动和本能反应。

lines.t: As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior.
lines.cn: 结果，我们任由纷扰的想法和情绪在意识中升起，并屈服于原始的行为。

lines.t: In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your senses are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous, and spontaneous.
lines.cn: 在情绪翻涌之时，请记住：情绪的产生是因为你的感官连接着心智中自我调节、自主而自发的原始部分。

lines.t: Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively.
lines.cn: 你理性的心智并不总能有效处理来自它的信息。

lines.t: These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses.
lines.cn: 这些信息是你生存机制的一部分，不该仅仅因为情绪“不健康”或暴露了你的软弱就被压抑。

lines.t: When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver.
lines.cn: 情绪出现时，不要压抑它们，而应关注它们，努力理解它们试图传递的信息。

lines.t: This way, you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability.
lines.cn: 这样，你就能在不失去平衡和内在稳定的前提下运用你的情绪。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Good morning class.
lines.cn: 同学们早上好。

lines.t: My topic today is how to feed a hungry world.
lines.cn: 我今天的主题是如何养活一个饥饿的世界。

lines.t: The world's population is expected to grow from 6.
lines.cn: 世界人口预计将从今天的 6.

lines.t: 8 billion today to 9.
lines.cn: 8 亿增长到 9.

lines.t: 1 billion by 2050.
Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007.
lines.cn: 与此同时，世界人口在 1961 至 2007 年间从 30 亿增长了一倍以上。

lines.t: Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research.
lines.cn: 同时，粮食生产一直因科研不足而受到制约。

lines.t: Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems easily possible.
lines.cn: 尽管如此，到 2050 年养活世界人口的任务似乎并不难完成。

lines.t: What is needed is a second green revolution.
lines.cn: 所需要的是第二次绿色革命。

lines.t: This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture.
lines.cn: 这是一种被描述为全球农业可持续增长的方式。

lines.t: Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research.
lines.cn: 这样的革命将要求农业研究的优先事项发生全面转变。

lines.t: There is an urgent need for new crop varieties.
lines.cn: 迫切需要新的作物品种。

lines.t: They must offer higher yields but use less water, nitrogen rich fertilizers, or other inputs.
lines.cn: 它们必须产量更高，却使用更少的水、氮肥或其他投入。

lines.t: These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat, and pests.
lines.cn: 这些新作物还必须更耐旱、耐热、抗虫。

lines.t: Equally crucial is lower tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms.
lines.cn: 同样关键的是针对基础问题的低技术研究，比如轮作，以及小农场上动植物的混合种养。

lines.t: Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices but that requires money.
lines.cn: 发展中国家可以通过更好地利用现代技术和做法，在生产效率上取得大幅提升，但这需要钱。

lines.t: It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to 83 billion U .
lines.cn: 据估计，为应对 2050 年的挑战，投资必须翻倍到每年 830 亿

lines.t: S.
lines.cn: 美

lines.t: dollars a year.
lines.cn: 元。

lines.t: Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure.
lines.cn: 其中大部分资金需要投向改善农业基础设施。

lines.t: Everything from production to storage and processing must improve.
lines.cn: 从生产到储存和加工的每个环节都必须改善。

lines.t: However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource-limited countries.
lines.cn: 然而，研究议程需要聚焦于最贫困、资源最有限的国家的需要。

lines.t: It is there that most of the world's population lives and it is there that population growth over the next decades will be the greatest.
lines.cn: 世界人口大部分生活在那里，未来几十年人口增长最快的也是那里。

lines.t: To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view.
lines.cn: 值得称赞的是，世界的农业科学家正在接受这样一种广阔的视野。

lines.t: In March, for example, they came together at the first global conference on agricultural research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations.
lines.cn: 例如，3 月他们齐聚首次全球农业研究大会，开始研究如何改变研究议程，以帮助满足较贫困国家农民的需要。

lines.t: But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policymakers.
lines.cn: 但除非得到政策制定者多得多的支持，这些计划不会开花结果。

lines.t: The growth in public agricultural research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since.
lines.cn: 公共农业研究支出的增长在 20 世纪 70 年代达到顶峰，此后一直在缩减。

lines.t: The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade.
lines.cn: 最大的例外是中国，过去十年其支出远超其他国家。

lines.t: China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries.
lines.cn: 中国似乎注定将转型为向较贫困国家提供相关科学技术的关键供应方。

lines.t: But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too.
lines.cn: 但发达国家同样有人道主义责任。

lines.t: Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified.
lines.cn: 科学家呼吁大幅增加公共农业研究的经费拨款，完全合理。
